causal_prompts: A wrought-iron tower rises from four curved legs joined by arches and narrows upward into stacked platforms and a spire.
The landmark shows an open lattice frame with a broad base, mid-level decks, and a sharply tapering vertical silhouette.
A long fortified wall follows mountain ridges with repeating crenellations and evenly spaced watchtowers.
The scene is identified by a continuous stone rampart that snakes across terrain in connected segments.
A seated woman is shown from the waist up with folded hands, direct gaze, and a calm half-smile.
The portrait composition features a frontal upper body, crossed hands in the foreground, and a centered human figure.
A massive naval ship has a long flat flight deck with runway markings and a side island superstructure.
The vessel is recognized by carrier layout: wide deck for aircraft operations atop a large warship hull.
A flying vehicle with a central fuselage, two fixed wings, tail fins, and engine units defines this class.
The object shows an aerodynamic body with wing span and rear stabilizers arranged for powered flight.
A compact timepiece body includes a clock face and distinct top bells or alarm controls.
The object is identified by a front dial with hour markers paired with an alarm mechanism on the casing.
A road vehicle with a boxy medical cabin, emergency markings, and roof signal units indicates patient transport.
The class appears as a van-like emergency vehicle configured for stretcher space and rapid response.
A human-like figure with prominent wings attached to the back forms the key identity cue.
The subject combines a person-shaped body and feathered wings, often in a poised or hovering posture.
Multiple animals move together in a common direction, forming a coordinated herd or flock pattern.
The event is recognized by collective locomotion of many animals with shared travel flow across space.
A tiny insect with three body segments, six legs, bent antennae, and a narrow waist is characteristic.
The class is marked by a segmented exoskeleton body plan with head, thorax, and abdomen linked in line.
A heavy metal block with a flat top, horn-shaped tapered end, and sturdy base defines this tool.
The object shows a forging surface and protruding beak profile used for shaping metal.
A round fruit body with smooth contour, a short stem at the top, and slight top-bottom dimples identifies it.
The class appears as a near-spherical pomaceous fruit with a central core region and stem attachment point.
An upper limb extends from shoulder to hand through upper arm, elbow joint, and forearm segments.
The body part is identified by a jointed long-limb structure ending in a wrist and hand.
Long green spears with straight stalks and compact bud-like tips are the defining visual feature.
The vegetable appears as slender shoots bundled by parallel stems and tapered heads.
A handle attached to a broad wedge-shaped cutting head forms the essential tool geometry.
The class is recognized by a long grip shaft ending in a sharpened metal blade for chopping.
A soft container with shoulder straps and a main zippered compartment worn on the back identifies this item.
The object shows a portable bag body with dual straps, top opening, and load-carrying pouch structure.
A curved elongated fruit with tapering ends and peel-separated sections marks this class.
The object is identified by crescent-like fruit geometry and a thick peel around soft inner flesh.
A narrow strip or patch used to cover injuries, often with an absorbent center, defines the item.
The class shows a protective wound-covering form with adhesive side regions around a central pad.
A large farm building with a high roof, wide doors, and storage-oriented interior volume is characteristic.
The structure is recognized by rural utility architecture featuring a broad rectangular body and pitched roofline.
A small spherical ball with stitched seam curves wrapping around the surface identifies it.
The object is defined by leather-covered ball geometry and distinct red seam patterning.
A smooth tapered club with a thick striking barrel and narrow grip handle defines this sporting tool.
The class appears as a long cylindrical bat with one hitting end and one handhold end.
An open-top container with raised sidewalls and a concave holding cavity is the key structure.
The object is identified by a bowl-like carrier form, often with a woven body and optional handle.
A round sports ball with black channel lines dividing orange-like panels is distinctive.
The class is recognized by a spherical ball marked by intersecting groove lines for grip and control.
A winged mammal with membranous wings stretched between elongated fingers and a small body defines it.
The animal shows outspread skin wings, pointed ears, and a hanging or flight-ready posture.
A large basin-shaped fixture with high sides and reclining interior space for bathing identifies this object.
The class appears as an elongated tub container designed to hold water for full-body washing.
